page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384gb is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic capabilities such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a minimal 1 GB NVMe SSD volume, and one public IPv4 address is provided without discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded execution and high memory throughput. The instance achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 2758.0 and a multi-core score of 26198.0, reinforced by a multi-core stress-ng rating of 88478.54. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by uncached read bandwidth of 395.69 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 231.13 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks. High-throughput data processing is further demonstrated by software compilation benchmarks registering 58607.0 in Clang, single-threaded gzip compression at 40.36 GB/sec, and Redis operations delivering 87.64 million SET operations per second.

The primary hardware tradeoff involves local storage capacity. While the platform offers substantial memory density and dedicated compute resources, the 1 GB local NVMe SSD functions primarily as a system footprint, requiring external or networked volumes for data persistence. The instance provides substantial cost efficiency for workloads that prioritize in-memory compute over attached local disk, including large in-memory databases, distributed caching deployments, continuous integration compilation tasks, and enterprise application backends.
